record.what_it_does: SP-API lets developers programmatically manage Amazon seller/vendor operations — orders, catalog, inventory, pricing, fulfillment, reports, feeds, finances, and notifications — on behalf of Amazon selling partners.
record.auth_notes: Public apps use OAuth 2.0 via Login with Amazon (LWA), with the selling partner authorizing through browser redirects; private (single-org) apps use a simplified 'self-authorization' flow through Seller/Vendor Central instead of a redirect flow. Every API call carries a short-lived LWA access token (bearer, x-amz-access-token header, 1hr expiry) obtained via refresh_token or client_credentials grants. Legacy AWS SigV4 request signing was sunset industry-wide, so LWA tokens are now the sole call credential.
record.access_notes: Registering as an SP-API developer in the Solution Provider Portal is free and doesn't require a paid selling plan. But public apps (the kind a multi-user agent toolkit would ship) must go through developer-profile review (security questionnaire, policy compliance) and, per the Solution Provider Agreement, must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore before broad production use; private apps additionally require a paid Professional selling account to self-authorize. Authorization Limits also cap roles/apps per developer.
record.main_blocker: public-app review and Appstore listing required for multi-user production access

record.open_questions: Amazon does publish an 'sp-api-dev-mcp' package under the amzn GitHub org, but it's an explicitly unsupported example (a local dev-assistant/workflow-builder tool with an sp_api_execute passthrough), not a hosted/official MCP server exposing SP-API operations as end-user agent actions — graded here as community/example-tier rather than a true 'official' MCP offering.
